To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystallinity of the disk is a direct probe of the formation history of the star and that the crystallinity, disk masses, and accretions rates are all related in a complex way.
the crystallinity of the dust is determined by the properties of the parent molecular cloud and that the crystallinity is a good tracer of disk formation history.
the level of crystallization is a sensitive probe of the formation history of a protoplanetary disk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the relationship between the level of crystallization of the dust, the disk mass, and the disk accretion rate?
understanding how the properties of a molecular cloud core affect the formation and evolution of the star+disk systems that it forms.
the question of whether the crystallinity in a disk reflects the properties of its parent molecular cloud core.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystalline silicate dust in the disk around a given star is an indirect probe of the properties of the cloud core in which the star was formed.
crystalline silicates in disks are an excellent probe of disk formation history.
the crystallinity of protoplanetary disks is not an indication of the age of the disk, but of the properties of the parent molecular cloud core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crystalline silicates can provide an important constraint on disk formation history, but the interpretation requires a detailed understanding of the underlying physics.
the crystalline silicates in protoplanetary disk can provide us a new perspective on how the disk formed and evolved.
the formation history of the molecular cloud and its fragmentation history is imprinted on the properties of the protoplanetary disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallinity of a given protoplanetary disk is a direct probe of the cloud core properties and thus the star+disk formation history.
the level of crystallization in a protoplanetary disk is a probe of the disk formation and evolution history.
the crystallinity of the dust is not a good tracer of disk evolution.
